source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Urgency of effect, client condition and ability to use the route, plus the medication's route-specific properties.","B":"Medication acquisition cost alone, because clinical urgency and route-specific pharmacology are lesser concerns.","C":"A single preferred route for all clients, because individual condition and medication properties rarely change selection.","D":"Client preference alone, because route safety, onset requirements, and drug properties do not affect route choice."}}
source_row.rationale: Medication route selection is clinical and drug-specific, considering desired onset, formulation/pharmacokinetics, patient condition, route feasibility and safety rather than cost or preference alone.
source_row.source_detail: Route-selection overview: route depends on drug properties, therapeutic objectives, patient condition and feasibility; routes differ in onset, bioavailability and practical limitations. NCBI Bookshelf StatPearls clinical reference rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: NCBI StatPearls — Medication Routes of Administration
source_row.stem: Which factor should most directly guide selection of a medication's route of administration?
